transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-07 14:00 UTC | Duration 42m | Attendees: Maya, Liam (Redwood)  Rajesh, Elena, Tom (Searchly)

Summary (auto): quick intro, then walkthrough of hosted embeddings + rerank. Demo of API, console, and a live rerank example using sample docs. Discussed tradeoffs, security, and next steps.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining  I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and Liam our solutions engineer is with me. How's it going over there?
[00:07] Rajesh: Good, thanks. Excited to see how this might improve our relevance. We're currently on Elastic with BM25 but results drift a lot as our catalog grows.
[00:13] Elena: Hi all, I'm Elena, I own the ranking models and pipelines. We need improvements especially for long-tail queries and semantic matches.
[00:20] Liam: Great, today's agenda is quick product tour of the hosted embeddings and rerank endpoints, show the console for monitoring, and run a live sample rerank. We'll leave some time for security and pricing. Sound good?
[00:29] Tom: Yep. Also curious about latency  our SLOs are 200ms p90 for search.
[00:34] Maya: Noted. Quick qual: volume and traffic shape?
[00:37] Rajesh: Right now about 1.2M queries per month, spikes during launches, p95 ~350ms on our elastic cluster, and infra ops is a pain. We want to keep cost predictable.
[00:47] Liam: Thanks  that helps. Ok demo  first, embeddings. Redwood hosted API can generate dense vectors via /v1/embeddings. You can choose models that balance cost/quality, and we provide batch endpoints for throughput.
[01:03] Liam: (shares screen) Here's the Console  index management, embedding stats, token-cost breakdown. You can see recent embedding generation metrics, token counts, and per-request latency. A note: tokenization and model names sometimes show slightly different tokens in the UI, small mismatch from auto transcriptions.
[01:20] Elena: Do you persist embeddings for us or do we push to our vector DB?
[01:24] Liam: You have options. For hosted quickstarts we persist snapshots in a secure store; most customers push embeddings to their preferred vector store. Redwood also integrates with managed vector stores or you can keep everything in your infra if you need residency.
[01:36] Rajesh: We prefer to keep vectors inside our VPC. Any constraints on that?
[01:40] Maya: For Private deployments we support VPC connectors and on-prem options; for Hosted we offer dedicated tenancy options and encryption at rest with KMS. We'll send the SOC2 and security whitepaper.
[01:49] Tom: Good. Can you speak to keys and rotation?
[01:52] Liam: API keys integrate with KMS; rotation is supported. For Private you can bring your own HSM.
[01:58] Liam: Now the rerank endpoint  architecture: you send candidate doc ids + context + query, we compute embeddings (or accept precomputed), run a lightweight neural re-ranking model and return a score and explanation tokens, along with latency guarantees depending on plan.
[02:15] Elena: Do you do prefix caching for repeated queries?
[02:18] Liam: We do KV cache for LM generation paths; for embeddings/rerank we have caching layers and can cache candidate embeddings and rerank responses for N minutes depending on cache policy. That reduces cost and latency for hot queries.
[02:29] (Liam pastes curl example)
[02:32] Liam: Example call: curl POST /v1/rerank with body {query, candidates: [{id, doc_embedding?}], model: "rr-small", return_scores: true}  returns ranked list with scores. You can also pass precomputed embeddings to skip generation.
[02:48] Rajesh: If we compute embeddings ourselves and store them, how much does rerank depend on external vector store?
[02:53] Liam: You can push embeddings to your store and pass candidate ids to rerank. Redwood can pull embeddings via connector or you can bundle embeddings in the rerank request. For latency-critical paths bundling embeddings increases payload size but avoids network hops. There's a tradeoff.
[03:09] Elena: What's typical p95 for rerank?
[03:12] Liam: On hosted standard it's around 60-120ms p95 for small rerank models when embedding generation is skipped or precomputed. If you ask Redwood to generate embeddings inline, add ~30-80ms depending on model and sequence length. For your 200ms p90 SLO we recommend precomputing embeddings and using the small reranker, or provision Dedicated capacity if you want stricter SLOs.
[03:34] Rajesh: Makes sense. Cost wise? We need per-1M query estimate.
[03:38] Maya: We'll include tailored pricing but rough guidance: embeddings cost per 1k vectors + rerank costs per 1k calls; batching and caching reduce effective cost by up to 40% in typical setups. We'll send numbers.
[03:49] Liam: Now demoing live rerank - I uploaded a small sample product catalog; I'm going to run a baseline BM25 (we replicated locally) then run Redwood rerank.
[03:59] (screen) [04:05] Liam: First query: "wireless noise cancelling headphones for travel"  BM25 top results show brand matches but miss some semantic intent.
[04:15] (typing)
[04:22] Liam: Now calling Redwood rerank with precomputed embeddings I pushed to the demo store. Response coming...
[04:28] (results)
[04:30] Liam: You can see rerank moves a result with better semantic match up in the list and we return scores  here's an explanation snippet: "semantic similarity 0.84, term match 0.12"  explanation output is approximate.
[04:46] Elena: I like that  shows better long-tail matches. Does the explanation include token-level alignments?
[04:51] Liam: We surface short explanation tokens and feature contributions; full transparency can be tuned for privacy.
[04:57] Rajesh: How do we measure regressions? We run A/B tests now.
[05:01] Maya: Console supports rollouts, canary, A/B split, and quality telemetry. You can tie alerts to evaluation suites and prompt sets. We'll show that in the trial.
[05:12] Tom: Any limits on candidate set size?
[05:15] Liam: Typical recommended candidate set is 50-200. Larger sets increase latency linearly; we provide cost/latency tradeoff guidance and have autoscaling and batching to help.
[05:26] Elena: Is there an SDK snippet for node/python?
[05:29] Liam: Yes  we have SDKs and a sample repo. I'll drop the link; example pseudo: client.rerank({query, candidates, model: 'rr-small'}) that's it.
[05:40] (Maya posts link to docs in chat)
[05:43] Rajesh: Security checklist  where to find SOC2, data residency, logs?
[05:47] Maya: We have SOC 2 Type II, ISO in progress, audit logs accessible via the Console, and optional log forwarding to your SIEM. For VPC/private we can do a private control plane and bring-your-own-key. We'll attach whitepaper.
[05:59] Tom: For compliance we need data retention controls and deletion APIs.
[06:03] Liam: Deletion APIs, retention windows, and audit trails are supported. We'll include sample retention config.
[06:12] (Small pause)
[06:15] Rajesh: Can you talk about backups and failover? If hosted region has issues, how do you handle high availability?
[06:21] Maya: Smart routing across regions and fallback to compatible model variants. For enterprise we offer dedicated pools + SLA-backed uptime. We'll outline HA in the security doc.
[06:32] Elena: Anything about model versioning? We want to pin a reranker version for consistency across A/B tests.
[06:36] Liam: You can pin model versions per route, and the Console tracks model rollout and regressions. We also support gradual rollouts and automatic rollback if quality drops.
[06:46] Rajesh: Ok, timeline  we want a pilot within two weeks and a benchmark within a month.
[06:51] Maya: Great. Next steps: I'll send pricing + enable a trial API key, Liam will run the initial rerank repro on your sample and share numbers, and Elena will send sample queries/docs.
[06:59] Tom: Sounds good. Anything else?
[07:02] Maya: Quick recap of risks/objections we heard  latency SLOs (we recommended precompute or dedicated), data residency (we propose VPC/dedicated or Private), and cost predictability (we'll show batching/caching knobs and recommend a pilot).
[07:15] Rajesh: Appreciate it.
[07:17] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the whitepaper and trial link by end of day.

(auto footer) Action items captured in CRM. Transcript ends.
